scene.headline: We left the neck
metadata: PARIS · ÉCOLE NORMALE SUPÉRIEURE · LOUIS PASTEUR
YEAST WATER · SWAN-NECK FLASKS · THE MER DE GLACE

counter.label: flasks spoiled on the Mer de Glace

connections.why: Pasteur came to living ferments from his tartrate crystals: microbes that fermented racemic acid ate one hand and left the other, part of the work on fermentation that led him to the flasks.

The flasks showed that microbes come from germs in the air, not from a spontaneous change in the liquid; the same reasoning told Pasteur that the diseases of wine were microscopic growths that heat could kill.
Lister built antiseptic surgery on what these flasks showed: that putrefaction comes not from the oxygen of the air but from living germs carried in it.
Pasteur took up the flasks because he held that fermentation is the work of living cells; Buchner's cell-free yeast juice later showed the work is done by enzymes inside them.
